title: Wiper instructions shipped inside an AI coding extension release
system: Amazon Q Developer extension for Visual Studio Code, v1.84.0
blast_radius: One released extension version, available for roughly 48 hours. The vendor reported no evidence that any customer environment suffered data deletion or disruption; the payload was reported to be non-functional due to a formatting error.
summary: An outside contributor submitted a commit that embedded instructions directing the coding agent to return a system to a near-factory state, deleting local files and cloud resources including object storage, compute instances and identity users. An inappropriately scoped build token allowed the commit to reach an official release. The malicious version shipped and remained available for roughly two days before being pulled. Severity here is rated on realised impact, not intent: the payload did not execute as written.
containment: Version pulled and replaced; the over-scoped credential was revoked and the release path tightened.

sources.title: Security Update for Amazon Q Developer Extension for Visual Studio Code (Version 1.84)
Amazon AI coding agent hacked to inject data wiping commands

scenario.description: Instructions bundled with the agent's own tooling drive a destructive local operation.
